design_systems.name: Aqua
principles: The look follows a water theme with droplet-like controls.
Controls use gel and glass effects with reflection and translucency.
Blue, white and gray are the main colours.
Animation, such as the Dock bounce and the Genie effect, gives feedback.

design_systems.name: Metro (Microsoft Design Language)
design_systems.licence: Not stated in the sources used
principles: Content comes before chrome. The interface has little decoration.
Large type and simple geometric icons carry the design.
Tiles stand for single units of information.
Public transport signs were one inspiration.
Motion gives natural feedback and a sense of depth.

design_systems.name: iOS 6 interface
principles: It was the last major iOS release with a skeuomorphic design.

design_systems.name: Atlassian Design System
design_systems.licence: Not stated in the sources used
principles: One design language makes every app feel the same and known.
Design tokens name colour, type and elevation by role.

design_systems.name: iOS 7 interface
principles: Apple described the icons as sharper and flatter, and the fonts as slimmer.
The design moved away from skeuomorphism.
A team under Jony Ive, then head of design, made the look.

design_systems.name: SAP Fiori
design_systems.licence: Not stated in the sources used

design_systems.name: Material Design
design_systems.licence: Apache-2.0 (Android and iOS code), BSD-3-Clause (Flutter), MIT (Web); guidelines proprietary to Google
principles: The interface uses a paper and ink metaphor: surfaces and layers that behave like physical material.
Interaction ideas come from skeuomorphism, but are applied in a more advanced way.

design_systems.name: Fluent 2
design_systems.licence: MIT (Fluent UI code); fonts and icons under a separate assets licence
principles: One Microsoft look across products, services and communities.
A token system helps handoff from design to code.
Corners are standard across components.
The colour system is more unified than in the first Fluent.

design_systems.name: Liquid Glass
principles: A translucent glass-like material refracts and reflects the content behind it.
Elements adapt to light or dark backgrounds to keep text and icons legible.
Motion is fluid and reacts to device movement on iOS and iPadOS.
Toolbars split into bubbles by context. App icons use layers.
